system_overview: This specification models the Boulangerie algorithm, a variant of Lamport's bakery algorithm for mutual exclusion, published by Yoram Moses and Katia Patkin at SIROCCO 2015. The Boulangerie algorithm improves on the bakery algorithm by eliminating unnecessary blocking: it analyzes how processes establish and detect priority, and allows a process to proceed when it can determine that another process has re-entered the doorway (and thus will choose a new, higher ticket number) or when it holds the lowest possible ticket number and only needs to check lower-numbered processes.
actors_and_components: The system consists of N concurrent processes (numbered 1 through N) that repeatedly cycle between a non-critical section, an entry protocol (doorway), a critical section, and an exit protocol. Each process independently competes for exclusive access to a shared critical section.
state_variables: The system tracks two shared arrays indexed by process identifier: (1) a ticket number for each process (zero means not competing), and (2) a boolean flag indicating whether the process is currently choosing its ticket number in the doorway. Each process also maintains local state for: a set of processes still to be checked during the waiting phase, the maximum ticket number observed during scanning, the identifier of the process currently being waited on, and the previously observed ticket number of the process being waited on (used to detect re-entry into the doorway).
initial_state: All ticket numbers are zero. All choosing flags are false. Each process starts in its non-critical section. The previously-observed-ticket variable for each process is initialized to a sentinel value indicating no previous observation.
actions: The algorithm proceeds in phases: (1) Entry/doorway: The process sets its choosing flag to true, scans all other processes to find the maximum ticket number, selects a ticket number equal to one plus that maximum, then sets its choosing flag to false. When clearing the flag, the set of processes to check during waiting is determined: if the chosen ticket number is 1 (the lowest possible non-zero value), only processes with lower identifiers need to be checked; otherwise, all other processes are checked. (2) Waiting: For each process in the set to be checked, the process first waits until the other process is not choosing. It then resets its record of the other process's previously observed ticket number. The process checks whether the other process can be skipped: it can be skipped if the other process's ticket number is zero, or if the current process has higher priority (lower lexicographic pair of ticket number and identifier), or if the other process's ticket number has changed since the last observation (indicating it re-entered the doorway and will choose a higher number). If the other process cannot yet be skipped, the current process records the other's ticket number and re-checks. (3) Critical section: The process executes its critical section. (4) Exit: The process resets its ticket number to zero. Nondeterminism is present in the entry and exit steps — flag and ticket number may be written multiple times with arbitrary intermediate values before settling, modeling non-atomic (safe register) writes.
safety_properties: Mutual exclusion: no two distinct processes may be in the critical section at the same time.
liveness_properties: Deadlock freedom: if any process is trying to enter the critical section, eventually some process enters. Starvation freedom: every process that begins trying to enter the critical section will eventually enter it.
model_bounds: The number of processes N is a constant natural number. For model checking, N must be instantiated with a specific finite value.
additional_assumptions: Weak fairness is assumed for each process when it is not in its non-critical section. The specification models safe registers (non-atomic reads and writes) through nondeterministic stuttering at entry and exit points. A formal machine-checked proof of mutual exclusion is included.
